A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have studied sequential allocation and optimal stopping for the problem of simultaneous estimation of two unknown parameters, and have derived a number of new and interesting results.

we have shown that the sequential allocation procedure of the optimal pair (policy, time) is a function of the posterior probabilities of θ1 and the posterior probability of θ2 and the posterior probability that the next observation will be an X, and that this procedure is asymptotically optimal.

we have shown that the optimal design for the problem of simultaneous estimation of θ _{1} and θ _{2} using additive estimation loss and a fixed budget, is the design which allocates the budget to the population with the larger variance, and that the asymptotically optimal design is the design which uses the ratio of variances to determine allocation, and stops when the sum of the variances is equal to the budget.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sequential allocation and stopping problem in simultaneous estimation is not a trivial extension of the sequential allocation and optimal stopping problem in single parameter estimation, but rather a problem of considerable complexity.
sequential allocation and optional stopping in Bayesian simultaneous estimation can be studied by means of the same methods as those for single parameter estimation.
